data.afterValueJson: {"text": "The proposed business change involves onboarding QA corrected value, a Malta-based card settlement processor, which will have access to sensitive customer data including cardholder Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and settlement files. Given this processor's jurisdiction in Malta and the nature of the data access scope, there is an inherent risk related to the confidentiality and security of customer information, particularly involving retail cardholders and Money Services Business (MSB) merchants. The delivery channel for settlement processing will be through API without face-to-face contact, which aligns with categories of products and services identified in the FFIEC BSA/AML Manual as vulnerable to money laundering risks due to rapid movement of funds and limited physical interaction (Risks Associated with Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing - Products and Services).", "riskCategoryId": "22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222"}

{"text": "The proposed change involves onboarding a Malta-based card settlement processor, QA corrected value, which will have access to cardholder PII and settlement files. This vendor will serve retail cardholders and MSB merchants through an API delivery channel, which is a non-face-to-face method. According to the FFIEC BSA/AML Manual on Risks Associated with Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, non-face-to-face delivery channels, including reliance on third-party agents or correspondent relationships to deliver products, reduce a bank's ability to verify customer identity and intent directly, thereby increasing risk (Delivery Channels). Given that Malta is the vendor jurisdiction, it is critical to consider the geographic risk factors associated with operating in or contracting with vendors in that location, as outlined in the supervisory citation for Geographic Locations.", "riskCategoryId": "22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222223"}

data.afterValueJson: {"text": "The onboarding of the Malta-based settlement vendor, QA corrected value, introduces specific risks related to the handling of cardholder PII and settlement files, accessed via an API-based, non-face-to-face delivery channel. Given the vendor's jurisdiction and the involvement of retail cardholders and MSB merchants, this change requires careful assessment under the FFIEC BSA/AML Manual's guidance on risks associated with customers and entities. Consistent with the policy section on Products and Services, the vendor's role facilitates rapid movement of funds and limited face-to-face interaction, both factors increasing money laundering vulnerability. The bank must ensure it has identified, measured, and implemented adequate risk mitigation controls before onboarding this service to address these inherent risks.", "riskCategoryId": "22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222"}
